newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar firmer as inflation fears subside.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar firmer as inflation fears subside.

text.p: * Canada's dollar opened stronger at C$1.3769 (US$0.7262) in light trading on Monday as inflation fears subsided and investors continued to buy Canadian assets on overseas markets, traders said. * They said U.S. data released Friday showing an unexpected drop in producer prices in May triggered a move to hold Canadian bonds and fixed income assets.

Analysts said the lower-than-expected producer prices data combined with weaker retail sales data had given the U.S. Federal Reserve little reason to hike U.S. rates at the next Federal Open Market Committee meeting in early July.

That scenario frees the Bank of Canada from pressure to hike Canadian rates and avoid widening interest rate spreads. "If the Fed is not going to go in July -- and I personally can't see how they would at this time -- this definitely opens the door for the Canada (dollar) to do a little better," said Reid Farrill, corporate foreign exchange adviser for CIBC Wood Gundy.
But Farrill cautioned that market sentiment was resigned to eventual Fed tightening later this year.
"It's still a market pre-disposed to thinking that ultimately the Fed will be raising rates in the not-so-distant future, so that caps the upside to the Canada (dollar)," Farrill said.

Analysts said the Canadian dollar would likely trade in a range of C$1.3740 (US$0.7278) and C$1.3790 (US$0.7251) ahead of U.S. consumer price data due to be released on Monday. A Reuter survey of economists forecast consumer prices in May will rise 0.2 percent.
Analysts said higher prices would renew speculation about rate hikes, while lower prices could rally the Canadian dollar to levels stronger than C$1.3700 (US$0.7299).
On the crosses, the Canada dollar dropped to 82.49 from Friday's 83.09 and dipped to 1.2553 marks from Friday's 1.2571 marks.
